_doc: Feasibility measurement for an `exec:` evidence form in the claims ledger (road-to-enforcement-proof Phase 5). The question this answers is NOT 'would exec: be nice' but 'would it cover enough of the ledger to earn its maintenance surface'. The threshold was pre-registered in the roadmap BEFORE this was measured: >= 10 percentage points of the backed ledger, or it gets parked with the number published. Measured 2026-07-25 against docs/CLAIMS.md.
measured_at: 2026-07-25 (re-counted twice; the first publication said 25 backed / 10 feasible and was measured mid-PR. The 11-feasible figure was then corrected DOWN to 10 when the form was actually built: context-token-reduction was counted feasible because check_token_regression re-derives token figures via js-tiktoken, but the script reads internal/bench/reports/projection-cost.json, which is gitignored as a per-run artifact — so the command is not self-sufficient in a fresh checkout and exits 1. Found by the exec: gate on its first CI run, which is the gate doing its job.
decision: JUSTIFIED — 40 pp clears the pre-registered 10 pp bar by a wide margin. `exec:` becomes its own PR; it is deliberately NOT built here, because the point of measuring first was to avoid shipping a schema change, a validator, and a renderer on an assumption.
method: Each backed entry was classified by whether a deterministic command could re-derive the claim with its exit code carrying the verdict. Pointing at a producer is not sufficient — a bench report whose regeneration needs paid model calls is not re-runnable in CI, and was counted NO. Two borderline cases were checked rather than assumed: measure_lexical_ranking.ts has zero model/API/fetch references (deterministic, model-free re-ranking), and token-baseline figures are re-derived by check_token_regression.ts via js-tiktoken. Both counted YES.

feasible.why: ratchet script; exit code IS the verdict
the same script re-derives the count the JSON snapshots
gate compares prose counts against source counts
ratchet built in Phase 1 of this roadmap
deterministic scan over the shipped tree
verified model-free — deterministic re-ranking of a fixed retrieved set
exact tokenizer over static surfaces; the headline token figures are re-derivable (the paired quality gate half is not, and is not claimed)
the pointer is a test assertion whose literal IS the count; running it re-derives the claim, and lint_surface_matrix independently holds the matrix in set-equality with the installer path map

honest_caveat: `exec_feasible` counts claims for which a re-running command PLAUSIBLY carries the verdict. It is not a promise that all ten pass on first wiring, and a claim whose command exits 0 for a reason unrelated to the claim would be a false green — argument hardening and a narrow prefix allowlist are what keep that from becoming the new hole.
ledger_hygiene_note: Found while counting: 10 entries filed under `## Unbacked inventory (documented debt)` carry `status: backed`. The checker keys on the status field, not the heading, so nothing is mis-gated — but the section headings no longer describe their contents and a reader would be misled. Filed for a follow-up pass, not silently fixed here.
_snapshot_note: backed_claims is a dated snapshot of the ledger, not a live read. It drifted once already. Re-count with: ./scripts-run src/scripts/check_claims (reports the live backed total) and re-classify feasibility by hand — the classification is a judgment, only the denominator is mechanical.

built.note: The pre-registered threshold was >= 10 pp. Measured 38.5 pp after correction, so the decision to build stands on the corrected number too — the over-count did not change the verdict, only the size of the margin.

over_counted.actual: NO — check_token_regression requires internal/bench/reports/projection-cost.json, which is gitignored and produced by `task audit-tokens`; a command with an uncommitted precondition cannot carry exec: standalone.
over_counted.disposition: reverted to its pointer form; listed as unfalsifiable-by-machine
